Nxeon (VPS/game-hosting business, production Next.js app at /opt/nxeon). The owner reviewed a live screenshot of the per-family game mods page (e.g. `/mods/games/sons-of-the-forest`, "Sons of the Forest mods & plugins") and flagged the SAME hero-layout bug that's being fixed elsewhere on the homepage hero right now: the game hero image renders letterboxed/constrained on the right side of the header block instead of stretching full-width, with plain text/stats to its left in a narrow column.

IMPORTANT: Multiple other background agents are concurrently working on NxLabs right now — one of them (still possibly running) is fixing this exact hero-treatment bug on the marketing `/mods` HOMEPAGE (full-bleed image + gradient overlay + particle effect, matching `.design-refs/nxlabs/hero-collage.png`/`marketing-home.png`), plus mod detail page hero art, plus a description backfill. Another is redesigning the mod card component. Another three are building import pipelines (GitHub/Thunderstore/Steam Workshop) — do not touch any import scripts or `worker/game-mods.ts`.

**Before you start**: run `git log --oneline -15` and `git status` to see what has already landed from the concurrent hero-fix work. If the homepage hero (`app/(marketing)/mods/page.tsx`) has ALREADY been redesigned with a full-bleed/overlay treatment, your job is to apply the SAME established pattern/component to the per-family page for consistency — read whatever component or CSS approach that commit introduced and reuse it, don't invent a second, different-looking hero treatment. If it hasn't landed yet (check timestamps/commit messages), read `.design-refs/nxlabs/marketing-home.png` yourself and build the same full-bleed-with-overlay treatment independently, keeping it simple enough that the other agent's later work can layer a particle effect on top without conflict — favor extracting the hero markup into a small shared component (e.g. a `NxLabsHero` component both the homepage and family pages import) if one doesn't already exist, since that would also make the homepage's fix automatically apply here.

## Scope
Fix the hero section specifically on:
- `app/(marketing)/mods/games/[family]/page.tsx` (marketing per-family page — the one in the screenshot)
- `app/dashboard/nxlabs/games/[family]/page.tsx` (portal equivalent — check `.design-refs/nxlabs/game-page-portal.png` for portal's intended treatment, which may legitimately differ from marketing's per portal shell constraints, same reasoning as the homepage portal/marketing split)

Do NOT touch: the mod card component (`components/mods/ModCard.tsx`, `components/mods/StoreBrowser.tsx`), mod detail pages (`[family]/[slug]/page.tsx`), any import scripts, or `worker/game-mods.ts`. Those belong to other concurrent agents.

Each family page's hero uses the real per-game art via `GAME_ART_SLUG[family].hero` (`lib/games.ts`) — that data plumbing is already correct (confirmed in earlier research), this is purely a layout/CSS fix: full-width/full-bleed image, a gradient/transparent overlay so the title+stats text sits legibly on top of or beside the art without the current cramped letterboxed look, matching the real approved mockup's actual proportions.

## Process (mandatory)
- Read both target files, `lib/games.ts`'s `GAME_ART_SLUG`, and whatever hero component/pattern exists (old or newly landed from the concurrent agent) in full before editing.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.
- Real Playwright before/after screenshots of at least 2 different family pages (to confirm the fix generalizes, not just hardcoded for one game) on both marketing and portal.
- Build via `bash scripts/deploy-staging.sh main` (never build directly in /opt/nxeon), verify staging HTTP 200 + visually correct, then `bash scripts/promote-production.sh`, confirm BUILD_ID changed + fresh service ActiveEnterTimestamp.
- Add a dated entry to `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md`.
- Commit; check `git log origin/main` before AND after to catch/reconcile any concurrent pushes from the sibling agents — re-pull and rebase if origin/main moved during your work rather than force-pushing over it.

Report back: whether you reused an already-landed shared hero pattern or built one fresh (and whether you extracted it into a shared component for future reuse), and confirm both marketing and portal family-page heroes render correctly live with real screenshots described.

#!/bin/bash
# Deploy a ref (default: main from /opt/nxeon) to the staging environment.
# Usage: ./scripts/deploy-staging.sh [git-ref]
set -euo pipefail
REF="${1:-main}"
cd /opt/nxeon-staging

echo "==> Syncing staging to $REF"
git fetch origin
git reset --hard "origin/$REF"

echo "==> Installing dependencies"
npm install --no-audit --no-fund 2>&1 | tail -1

echo "==> Applying database schema"
npx prisma db push --accept-data-loss 2>&1 | tail -2
npm run db:seed 2>&1 | tail -2 || true

echo "==> Building"
npm run build 2>&1 | tail -4

# next.config sets output:"standalone" but the systemd unit runs the standalone
# server.js directly (not `next start`, which Next.js explicitly does not
# support alongside output:"standalone" — it prints a warning and silently
# fails to resolve some routes, confirmed live 2026-09-10: a brand-new API
# route 404'd under `next start` on this exact build and returned 200 under
# `node .next/standalone/server.js`). The standalone output does NOT include
# public/ or .next/static/ (Next's own documented behavior) — copy them in
# fresh every build, or every static asset/route added after the last copy
# is missing until the next deploy happens to also touch this step.
echo "==> Copying static assets into the standalone server output"
rm -rf .next/standalone/public .next/standalone/.next/static
cp -r public .next/standalone/public
cp -r .next/static .next/standalone/.next/static
# geoip-lite is in next.config.ts's serverExternalPackages (kept OUT of the JS
# bundle on purpose, since it reads .dat files off its own package path at
# runtime) — but the standalone output tracer only copies files it can trace
# as JS-imported, so an externalized package's own non-JS data files are
# silently left behind. Found live 2026-09-10: this crashed EVERY request
# with an uncaught ENOENT the moment the systemd unit ran the standalone
# server.js instead of `next start` — geo-ip.ts's own try/catch around
# geoip.lookup() does NOT help, because the failure isn't confined to that
# call. Copy the package's real data/ directory in every build, same
# reasoning as public/.next/static above.
if [ -d node_modules/geoip-lite/data ]; then
  mkdir -p .next/standalone/node_modules/geoip-lite/data
  cp -r node_modules/geoip-lite/data/. .next/standalone/node_modules/geoip-lite/data/
fi

# Web runs as the unprivileged 'nxeon' user. Only .next needs to be writable by
# it (Next cache); the rest stays root-owned and world-readable, and systemd
# injects .env as root. Do NOT chown the whole tree (breaks root git on .git).
echo "==> Fixing .next ownership for non-root web"
chown -R nxeon:nxeon /opt/nxeon-staging/.next 2>/dev/null || true
chmod 600 /opt/nxeon-staging/.env 2>/dev/null || true

echo "==> Restarting staging services"
systemctl restart nxeon-staging-web nxeon-staging-worker
sleep 5
systemctl is-active nxeon-staging-web nxeon-staging-worker
CODE=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1:8080/)
echo "==> Staging responds: HTTP $CODE (http://$(grep ^PUBLIC_IP .env | cut -d= -f2):8080)"
[ "$CODE" = "200" ] || { echo "STAGING UNHEALTHY"; exit 1; }
echo "==> Staging deploy complete"

# group-readable. Do NOT chown the whole tree (breaks root git on .git).

chown -R nxeon:nxeon /opt/nxeon/.next 2>/dev/null || true
chown nxeon:nxeon /opt/nxeon/.env 2>/dev/null || true
chmod 600 /opt/nxeon/.env 2>/dev/null || true

systemctl restart nxeon-web

# mid-provision used to interrupt a live VM build and (with a non-idempotent retry)
# strand the server in ERROR. The start step is now idempotent so this is
# belt-and-suspenders, but avoiding the interruption entirely is cleaner. Bounded
# wait (max ~4 min) so a deploy can never hang forever.
DBURL=$(grep -E '^DATABASE_URL=' /opt/nxeon/.env | head -1 | cut -d= -f2- | tr -d '"')
if [ -n "$DBURL" ] && command -v psql >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  for _ in $(seq 1 24); do
    ACTIVE=$(psql "$DBURL" -tAc "SELECT count(*) FROM \"Job\" WHERE status='RUNNING' AND type='PROVISION';" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '[:space:]')
    [ "${ACTIVE:-0}" = "0" ] && break
    echo "==> Waiting for ${ACTIVE} in-flight provision(s) to finish before restarting worker…"
    sleep 10
  done
fi

echo "==> Restarting production worker"
systemctl restart nxeon-worker
sleep 5
systemctl is-active nxeon-web nxeon-worker
CODE=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1/)
echo "==> Production responds: HTTP $CODE"
